mainTopic: Proofs for רב גידל about unfit sprinkling and מעילה, and רבי יהושע's rule about שעת היתר לכהנים.
overview: The גמרא tries to prove רב גידל's view that sprinkling the blood in an unfit way does not take a קרבן out of מעילה. First it brings the סיפא of a ברייתא: blood left overnight and then sprinkled is still under מעילה. That case must be about a חטאת, since for an עולה it would be obvious. The גמרא then pulls back, because הלנה is a problem made through action, while פיגול is only a wrong thought. Next it tries a ברייתא saying פיגול of קדשי קדשים has מעילה. The answer that this means before sprinkling seems to fail, because then the ברייתא should have split before and after sprinkling. That proof is also pushed aside, since קדשים קלים may simply be the clearer contrast. The גמרא then turns to רבי יהושע's rule in the משנה: an offering that was once permitted to the כהנים has no מעילה, and one that never was permitted keeps מעילה. The משנה gives examples of each. The amud ends as בר קפרא begins to ask whether this 'permission' means permission from a proper שחיטה, a question that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Another proof from the end of the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a second proof for רב גידל from the סיפא of the ברייתא: blood left overnight and then sprinkled still leaves the קרבן under מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, the end of the ברייתא teaches: if its blood was left overnight, even though he later sprinkled it, one is still liable for מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another proof for רב גידל, this time from the last part (סיפא) of the ברייתא. It quotes the case of blood that was left overnight and only sprinkled afterward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blood left overnight becomes unfit for sprinkling. The ברייתא says that even if the כהן sprinkled it anyway, the קרבן is still under מעילה. That matches רב גידל's view that an unfit sprinkling does not remove מעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore: introduces an additional proof
The latter part of a משנה or ברייתא
Left overnight. Blood left past its time becomes unfit
One is liable for מעילה, the misuse of הקדש property

phrases.english: And furthermore, as the latter clause teaches:
If its blood was left overnight,
even though he later sprinkled it,
one is liable for misuse of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second proof for רב גידל after the earlier attempt from the רישא of the same ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רב גידל's ruling that an unfit sprinkling does not take a קרבן out of מעילה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The סיפא of the ברייתא: blood left overnight and then sprinkled is still subject to מעילה.

steps.title: Why the ending must be about a חטאת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows the proof works: the סיפא only makes sense for a חטאת, since for an עולה the ruling would be obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is talking about a חטאת, that works well. But if you say it is talking about an עולה, would it need to be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the סיפא really is a proof. It must be talking about a חטאת, because for an עולה there would be nothing new to teach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עולה is never given to the כהנים, so it stays under מעילה no matter what. Teaching that it stays under מעילה would be pointless. A proper sprinkling of a חטאת does take it out of מעילה, because the meat becomes permitted to the כהנים. So the ברייתא must be teaching that an unfit sprinkling of a חטאת does not do this, which is exactly רב גידל's view.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted, it works out well. Sets up a contrast with a version that does not work
Fine, it works well
Sin offering. After a proper sprinkling its meat is eaten by כהנים
Burnt offering. It is entirely burned and never permitted to כהנים
Does it need to be said? Meaning it would be obvious

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the ברייתא is saying an עולה is not under מעילה. An עולה is always under מעילה. That is exactly why the ruling would be pointless for it, and so the ברייתא must mean a חטאת.

phrases.english: Granted, if you say it is about a sin offering,
it is well.
But if you say it is about a burnt offering,
does it need to be said?
phrases.notes: An עולה is under מעילה even after a proper sprinkling, so there would be nothing new here.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the quoted סיפא really proves רב גידל's point.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ruling would be obvious for an עולה, so the סיפא must be talking about a חטאת.

steps.title: The ending clearly supports רב גידל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the סיפא definitely supports רב גידל.
steps.simpleTranslation: The latter clause certainly supports him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the proof. The end of the ברייתא definitely backs up רב גידל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the סיפא must be about a חטאת, it seems to clearly teach that an unfit sprinkling does not take the קרבן out of מעילה. For now the גמרא treats this as a solid proof, but step 5 will take it back.

keyTerms.meaning: Certainly, definitely
It supports him

steps.whatToRemember: At first, the סיפא (blood left overnight, then sprinkled) looks like a solid proof for רב גידל. Step 5 shows why it may not apply to פיגול.

phrases.english: The latter clause certainly supports him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms the proof built in steps 1 and 2.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The סיפא of the ברייתא definitely supports רב גידל.

steps.title: Does the beginning also support him?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the רישא (about פיגול) should also be read as supporting רב גידל, since the סיפא does.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about the first clause? Since the latter clause supports him, does the first clause also support him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns back to the first part (רישא) of the ברייתא and asks a question. This sets up the next discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רישא says פיגול is always under מעילה, and on its own it could be about an עולה. The question is whether we should read the רישא as being about a חטאת too, just because the סיפא is. If we do, it would be another support for רב גידל.

keyTerms.meaning: The first part of a משנה or ברייתא
Since, because
Also

phrases.english: The first clause, what about it?
phrases.notes: The רישא is the line in this ברייתא that פיגול is always under מעילה.

phrases.english: Since the latter clause supports him,
does the first clause also support him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After securing the סיפא, the גמרא goes back to the רישא, which was discussed earlier.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the רישא should also be read as being about a חטאת, and so as supporting רב גידל, because the סיפא is.

steps.title: Even the latter clause does not clearly support רב גידל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא retracts. Even the סיפא is not a sure proof, because הלנה is done with an action and פיגול is only a thought.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even the latter clause does not certainly support him. Why is leaving the blood overnight different? There the problem comes from an action, so sprinkling does not take the קרבן out of מעילה. With a wrong thought there is no action, so sprinkling might take it out of מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes back the proof from the סיפא. It explains that blood left overnight and פיגול may not be the same kind of problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 3 the סיפא seemed to prove רב גידל. Now the גמרא says that case was about הלנה, a problem created by something physically done (or left undone). פיגול comes only from a wrong intention, so sprinkling might still work there and take the קרבן out of מעילה, which is the opposite of what רב גידל holds.

keyTerms.meaning: Certainly, for sure
Leaving the blood overnight, which disqualifies it
Literally 'with hands': through a real action
A thought or intention, here the wrong intention that makes a קרבן פיגול
To take the item out of the laws of מעילה (misusing holy property)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two problems. הלנה is a physical problem with the blood. פיגול is a problem in the כהן's mind. The whole rejection rests on that difference.

phrases.english: The latter clause does not certainly support him:
phrases.notes: 'Him' is רב גידל. The גמרא is taking back what it said in step 3.

phrases.english: Why is leaving overnight different?
Because it is done through an action,
sprinkling is not effective
to remove it from the status of מעילה.
A wrong intention is not done through an action,
so sprinkling is effective for it
to remove it from the status of מעילה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Instead of answering whether the רישא also supports רב גידל, the גמרא withdraws even the proof from the סיפא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the סיפא (blood left overnight) for רב גידל
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: הלנה is a disqualification through action, while פיגול is only through thought, so a ruling about הלנה cannot be applied to פיגול.

steps.title: A new proof: פיגול in קדשי קדשים is subject to מעילה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings another ברייתא saying פיגול in קדשי קדשים is subject to מעילה, apparently even after sprinkling.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say this supports him: a פיגול offering of קדשי קדשים is subject to מעילה. Doesn't that mean even though the blood was sprinkled? Then it supports him!
steps.whatsHappening: Having lost the first proof, the גמרא tries a different ברייתא to support רב גידל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא speaks directly about פיגול, so the הלנה-versus-thought difference from step 5 does not matter here. If it means the קרבן stays under מעילה even after the blood was sprinkled, it matches רב גידל exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: A קרבן made invalid by the כהן's wrong intention about when it will be eaten
The most holy קרבנות, like עולה and חטאת
One who benefits from it is guilty of מעילה
He sprinkled (the blood on the מזבח)

phrases.english: Let us say this supports him:
A פיגול offering of the most sacred order,
one is liable for misusing it.
Does this not mean even though he sprinkled,
and so it supports him!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting the proof from הלנה, the גמרא looks for a source that speaks about פיגול itself.
steps.raayaObject: רב גידל's view that sprinkling a פיגול קרבן does not take it out of מעילה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: הפיגול בקדשי קדשים מועלין בו

steps.title: The ברייתא may mean before the blood was sprinkled
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof: the ברייתא may be talking about a case where the blood was not yet sprinkled.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it means where he did not sprinkle.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the new proof in just a few words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before sprinkling, a קרבן of קדשי קדשים is surely still under מעילה. So the ברייתא might only be teaching that, and it says nothing about what happens after sprinkling, which is the real question.

keyTerms.meaning: Where he did not sprinkle the blood

phrases.english: No, it is where he did not sprinkle.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from הפיגול בקדשי קדשים מועלין בו
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא can be read as a case before זריקה, so it proves nothing about after זריקה.

steps.title: Challenge from the סיפא about קדשים קלים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the rejection: if it is before sprinkling, why does the סיפא contrast this with קדשים קלים, where there is no מעילה?
steps.simpleTranslation: But if he did sprinkle, what? Is it true that there is no מעילה? Then why does the latter clause teach: in קדשים קלים there is no מעילה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the answer from step 7 by looking at how the same ברייתא ends.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the רישא is only about before sprinkling, then after sprinkling a פיגול of קדשי קדשים would have no מעילה. In that case, why does the ברייתא go to a different category, קדשים קלים, to show a case of no מעילה? The next step spells out the simpler way it could have taught this.

keyTerms.meaning: Lesser holy קרבנות, like שלמים
There is no מעילה for benefiting from it
Is it really so?

phrases.english: But if he did sprinkle, what is the law?
Is it really that one is not liable for misusing it?
Why does the latter clause teach:
In offerings of lesser sanctity, one is not liable for misusing it?
phrases.notes: This is the second half of the same ברייתא from step 6.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל זָרַק, מַאי? הָכִי נָמֵי דְּאֵין מוֹעֲלִין בּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the rejection in step 7 using the end of the same ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading in step 7 that the ברייתא is about a case before זריקה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If after sprinkling there were no מעילה in קדשי קדשים, the ברייתא would not need to bring קדשים קלים as its example of no מעילה. It could have split before and after sprinkling inside the רישא (step 9).

steps.title: Why not split before and after sprinkling inside the first case?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא spells out its challenge. If sprinkling made a difference, the ברייתא should have taught 'before sprinkling there is מעילה, after sprinkling there is not' within קדשי קדשים itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the ברייתא make the distinction in the first clause and teach: before sprinkling, there is מעילה; after sprinkling, there is no מעילה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the comparison to קדשים קלים in step 8 is a problem. A simpler and clearer way to teach the rule was available.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 said the ברייתא might be talking only about before sprinkling. If so, the natural contrast would be before versus after sprinkling, not קדשי קדשים versus קדשים קלים. Since the ברייתא did not teach that contrast, it seems to hold that there is מעילה in פיגול of קדשי קדשים even after sprinkling.

keyTerms.meaning: Sprinkling (throwing) the blood on the מזבח
There is liability for מעילה, meaning misusing הקדש
Let it make a distinction

phrases.english: Let it distinguish in the first clause, and teach:
phrases.notes: The 'first clause' is the part of the ברייתא about קדשי קדשים.

phrases.english: Before sprinkling, one is liable for misusing it,
after sprinkling, one is not liable for misusing it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the challenge begun in step 8 by showing the better way the ברייתא could have taught it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rejection in step 7, which said the ברייתא is talking about before sprinkling
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the case were only before sprinkling, the ברייתא should have contrasted before and after sprinkling within קדשי קדשים, not compared to קדשים קלים.

steps.title: The latter clause certainly supports רב גידל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that this part of the ברייתא definitely supports רב גידל.
steps.whatsHappening: After the challenge in step 9, the גמרא declares that this clause is a solid support for רב גידל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rejection in step 7 has been knocked down. The ברייתא's choice to contrast with קדשים קלים shows that, in its view, sprinkling does not remove מעילה from פיגול of קדשי קדשים.

keyTerms.meaning: Certainly, definitely
Supports him (backs up his view)
That one (that clause)

phrases.english: That one certainly supports him.
phrases.notes: 'Him' is רב גידל, and 'that one' is the latter clause of the ברייתא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the challenge in step 9.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For now, the ברייתא's latter clause is treated as clear support for רב גידל.

steps.title: Does the first clause support him too?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: since the סיפא supports רב גידל, should we say the רישא supports him as well?
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say: since the latter clause supports him, the first clause also supports him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests whether the support can be stretched to the other half of the ברייתא. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This repeats the move from step 4. If one clause backs רב גידל, perhaps the whole ברייתא does. As in step 5, the question leads to a pushback (step 12) that weakens even the proof from the סיפא in step 10.

keyTerms.meaning: Since, because
The latter (end) clause
The first (opening) clause

phrases.english: Shall we say: since the latter clause supports him,
the first clause also supports him?

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא הוֹאִיל וּמְסַיַּיע לֵיהּ סֵיפָא מְסַיַּיע לֵיהּ נָמֵי רֵישָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the conclusion of step 10 and asks whether it extends further.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the first clause of the ברייתא is also proof for רב גידל

steps.title: Even the latter clause is no proof: קדשים קלים is clear-cut
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pulls back. The ברייתא picked קדשים קלים as its contrast because that case has one simple rule. קדשי קדשים does not, so the contrast proves nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: With קדשים קלים, the rule is clear-cut. Here, it is not clear-cut.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes back its proof, just as it did in step 5. Even the סיפא does not surely support רב גידל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In קדשים קלים, פיגול never has מעילה, so it is a clean contrast. In קדשי קדשים the rule changes depending on sprinkling, so the ברייתא preferred the clean contrast. That choice no longer shows that sprinkling makes no difference.

keyTerms.meaning: It is clear-cut for him (one rule with no exceptions)
Offerings of lesser holiness, like שלמים
Here

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא now says sprinkling definitely removes מעילה. It only says this ברייתא can no longer prove either side.

phrases.english: Offerings of lesser sanctity are clear-cut for him,
phrases.notes: In קדשים קלים, פיגול never has מעילה, with no exceptions.

phrases.english: here, it is not clear-cut for him.
phrases.notes: 'Here' means קדשי קדשים, where the rule depends on whether the blood was sprinkled.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָדָשִׁים קַלִּים פְּסִיקָא לֵיהּ, הָכָא לָא פְּסִיקָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 11 by undoing even the proof from step 10.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the latter clause, and so from the whole ברייתא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא may have chosen קדשים קלים as its contrast only because it is the simpler case, not because sprinkling makes no difference.
steps.whatToRemember: In the end, neither ברייתא clearly proves רב גידל's view. Each proof was pushed aside.

steps.title: רבי יהושע's rule: once permitted to the כהנים, no מעילה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה. If an offering ever had a time when the כהנים were allowed to eat it, there is no מעילה. If it never had such a time, there is מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע stated a general rule: any offering that had a time of being permitted to the כהנים has no מעילה. Any offering that never had a time of being permitted to the כהנים has מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new section begins. The גמרא quotes רבי יהושע's general rule from the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מעילה applies to things that belong only to הקדש. Once an offering became permitted for the כהנים to eat, it left that category. It keeps that status even if it later becomes disqualified.

keyTerms.meaning: A general rule
A time when it was permitted (to be eaten)
Priests

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule is the key that decides when a disqualified offering still carries מעילה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua stated a general rule:

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁהָיְתָה לָהּ שְׁעַת הֶיתֵּר לַכֹּהֲנִים –
phrases.english: anything that had a time of being permitted to the priests,
one is not liable for misusing it,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֹל שֶׁלֹּא הָיְתָה לָהּ שְׁעַת הֶיתֵּר לַכֹּהֲנִים –
phrases.english: and anything that did not have a time of being permitted to the priests,
one is liable for misusing it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה after the discussion about רב גידל ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An offering that was once permitted to the כהנים has no מעילה. One that never was permitted to them has מעילה.

steps.title: Which offerings had a time of being permitted to the כהנים
steps.stepSummary: The משנה explains its rule with examples. These are an offering left overnight, one that became טמא, and one that left the courtyard.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which offering had a time of being permitted to the כהנים? One that stayed overnight, one that became טמא, and one that went out of the courtyard.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה asks itself a question and answers it. It lists the cases that fit רבי יהושע's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In all three cases the offering was first brought properly, so the כהנים were allowed to eat it. Only afterward did it become disqualified. That is why there is no מעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: Which one is it?
It stayed overnight past its time limit
It became ritually impure (טמא)
It went out of its allowed area (the courtyard)

phrases.aramaic: אֵיזוֹהִי שֶׁהָיְתָה לָהּ שְׁעַת הֶיתֵּר לַכֹּהֲנִים?
phrases.english: Which is the one that had a time of being permitted to the priests?
One that stayed overnight, and one that became impure, and one that went out.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיזוֹהִי שֶׁהָיְתָה לָהּ שְׁעַת הֶיתֵּר לַכֹּהֲנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives concrete examples of the rule stated in step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Offerings disqualified by לינה, טומאה, or יציאה after being properly offered had a time of being permitted, so there is no מעילה.

steps.title: Examples of offerings that never had a permitted time
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists offerings that never had a time when the כהנים could eat them: slaughtered with intent beyond its time, slaughtered with intent outside its place, or blood received and sprinkled by unfit people.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which offering never had a time when it was permitted to the כהנים? One slaughtered with the intention to eat it beyond its time or outside its place, or one whose blood was received and sprinkled by people unfit for Temple service.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now gives the other side of its rule: examples of offerings that were never permitted to the כהנים, so they stay under מעילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 14 the problem came after the offering was already permitted, like being left overnight or becoming טמא. Here the problem happens before the blood is properly sprinkled. So the meat was never permitted for one moment, and it stays fully holy with מעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: A time when the offering was permitted to be eaten
An intention to eat or offer it after its proper time
An intention to eat or offer it outside its proper area
People who are not fit to do Temple service
Sprinkling the blood on the מזבח, which makes the meat permitted

steps.whatToRemember: Problem after the offering was permitted: no מעילה. Problem before it was ever permitted: מעילה stays.

phrases.english: And which is the one that did not have
a time of permission for the priests?
One that was slaughtered beyond its time,
phrases.notes: He means slaughtered with the intention of eating or offering it after its proper time.

phrases.english: or outside its place,
or one where unfit people received
and sprinkled its blood.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵיזוֹהִי שֶׁלֹּא הָיְתָה לָהּ שְׁעַת הֶיתֵּר לַכֹּהֲנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite examples to step 14: offerings that never had a permitted time.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Offerings disqualified before they became permitted (wrong intent about time or place, or blood handled by unfit people) never had a permitted time, so מעילה applies.

steps.title: בר קפרא prepares his nephew for a question
steps.stepSummary: בר קפרא tells בר פדת to think carefully about the question he will ask tomorrow: does 'permission' in the משנה mean permission from the slaughtering?
steps.simpleTranslation: בר קפרא said to בר פדת: My sister's son, think about what you will ask me tomorrow in the בית המדרש. Did we learn permission of slaughtering?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a question about the משנה's words 'a time of permission.' This step opens the question; its second half comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is what counts as the moment of 'permission.' One option, given here, is that a proper שחיטה is enough, even if the offering became disqualified before the blood was sprinkled. The other side of the question comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: Permission that comes from a proper slaughtering
My sister's son, my nephew
The study hall

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not finished here. Don't assume the answer is 'שחיטה'; the גמרא is only listing the first possibility.

My sister's son,
look into what you will ask me
